newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cartel boss gives Mexico the slip again.
newsitem.headline: Cartel boss gives Mexico the slip again.

text.p: Mexico claimed a big success on Tuesday in its war on drugs after arresting more than 25 suspects linked to the country's top drug cartel but the ring's shadowy leader seemed to have escaped.

The Attorney-General's office (PGR) said the suspects included police who guarded a wedding last Saturday in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, apparently for the sister of Juarez cartel boss Amado Carrillo Fuentes. Also seized were three jets used to transport guests to the wedding.

Pilots of two of the planes confessed to having flown a group of people including heavily armed men wearing PGR uniforms and bullet-proof vests, two women and two children to the Sinaloa state capital of Culiacan, the PGR said.
Authorities said their suspicions were aroused when the jets left an airport near Mexico City for Sinaloa -- an area much frequented by traffickers -- without filing flight plans.
"This is a big step forward," said a source at the Attorney-General's office. "We are attacking the country's top cartel with a heavy blow".

Mexican law enforcement officials refused to give any more information beyond a brief PGR statement released on Monday night. Miguel Angel Ortega, deputy head of the Sinaloa PGR office, said only that the suspects were arrested early on Sunday morning and would be charged with firearms offences.

The PGR statement made no mention of Carrillo Fuentes himself. But at least two newspapers, quoting local sources, said he had attended the wedding and slipped away before the army arrived early on Sunday.

Nicknamed the "Lord of the Skies" for a propensity to ship planeloads of cocaine into Mexico from South America in converted jets, Carrillo Fuentes is Mexico's most wanted drug lord. He reportedly escaped a hit by a rival drug lord in a restaurant in 1994 by climbing out of a bathroom window while assassins peppered his fellow traffickers with bullets.

Described by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) as "the most powerful man in the Mexican drug trade", Carrillo Fuentes has been a fugitive for eight years and is the subject of 26 separate DEA investigations.

But despite the importance of Carrillo Fuentes and his cartel, centred on the border town of Ciudad Juarez, Mexican anti-drug operations in recent months had seemed to concentrate on the rival Tijuana cartel run by the Arellano Felix brothers.
Mexican commentators hailed the raid on the wedding as one of the first fruits of greater army involvement in the war on drugs, noting that during the operation soldiers had arrested corrupt police.

Those arrested included 12 municipal police allegedly providing security for the wedding and two state detectives. Two other suspects were carrying fake federal police credentials, while 11 others had no apparent police connection, the PGR said.
Its statement said 25 people were arrested but the individual numbers mentioned added up to 27. There was no explanation for the discrepancy.

President Ernesto Zedillo has named drug trafficking as the top threat to Mexican national security and appointed a hardline general to head the country's equivalent of the DEA, the National Institute for the Combat of Drugs (INCD).
Soldiers are also being used increasingly for drug raids to combat the corruption of Mexican federal police, many of whom in the past have been on the payroll of drug lords.
